_about: Source of truth for this file's names, enums and rooms. See chapters/ch2/chapter.json for the full note. Scene order is the enum order: the index in this list is the value Rive stores.

scene.about: Which room the stage shows. Setting the same value again does nothing.

direction.about: forward for Next, back for Back. Set before scene.

scenes.name: loading
scenes.about: The file's default and the Start room before its bird arrives: the empty cream-and-orange room with the standard ball bouncing in the centre. It has no room of its own; the Start room draws it. Not a card; when scene becomes start the ball finishes its bounce, then the bird drops in (no pan, no colour change).

scenes.name: ad
scenes.about: The empty Chapter 1 room: no props, no ball. Ad 1 and Ad 2 play here, and it is the picture File 2 opens on (File 2's from-chapter-1).

tuneLater: **Card 1: the ball's story is this scene's loop** (762 frames, 12.7 s), and the only scene that follows the scene loop guideline so far. It starts the moment the intro ends: the ball slides out of the cuckoo clock's door along the blue perch, bounces on the chair and onto the window, the nine panes flip to tiles and back (the ball is knocked off), and it rolls off the right edge. Once it is out of sight it is removed (put back behind the clock door, also out of sight); 3 s later it slides out again, and the loop repeats. The ball never goes beyond x 1519, so it always leaves with its room. The small loops (their own "Chapter 1 Card 1 Small" layer, which starts when the pan ends) fit the loop with no jump: the minute hand turns twice (24 ticks), the pendulum swings 12 times, the dog's tail wags 3 times, the mouse runs once and waits in its hole, one set of clouds drifts across the whole window (hidden while the panes are tiles), the plant sways and drifts, and the dog's eye follows the mouse (it closes as the mouse approaches, stays closed while the mouse passes, opens once the mouse is past on its way home, and blinks while open). To tune: the shift per contact (the clock, shelf, chair, window, dog bed and floor each have their own), the pause (3.03 s), the eye's timing against the mouse, the dog's tail speed and the clouds' speed.

**Card 1: the ball's turning** (audited against the new global rule, 2026-11-02). The ball already rolled correctly (Ball Art rotation: one turn per circumference, clockwise rolling right, anticlockwise rolling left, constant spin in the air). The only change: on the window (loop 1.8 to 2.4 s) and on the dog bed (4.5 to 5.0 s) the ball rests but its rotation wobbled by up to 0.17 radians; those two windows are now held still (a ball at rest stops turning). Nothing else about the story or its timing changed.
**Card 1: the dog's eye.** It is asleep while the mouse is in front of it. If it still doesn't read as asleep, the next step is a bigger cue (the head dipping, or a small z).

**Card 2: seesaw, slide down, climb back up** (finesse round 4, 2026-11-02; loop 462 frames, 7.7 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, and each later loop repeats them 7.7 s apart). The journey starts inside the intro, 2.02 s, as soon as the top block has landed. Intro: the ball sits on the pink and orange block and rides it down (squash when it lands, 1.63 s); the pencil tips into place quickly, 1.95 to 2.25 s with a bounce to 2.6 s. The slide: the block teeters on its white joint from 2.02 s (it rocks left, right, left), tips at 2.45 to 2.7 s and the ball rolls off its right end at 2.83 s (the block rocks back and settles); it lands on the purple bar at 3.2 s (the bar dips, the domino wobbles), rolls down it over the right white joint (it squashes), meets the pencil at the bar's low end at 3.35 s (the pencil gives a little), touches the joint's shoulder at 3.55 s, lands on the yellow stick at 3.85 s (it flexes), rolls across the slabs to the lower-left joint at 4.18 s (it squashes), slides down TOTAL's left edge from 4.42 s (the card is pressed 4 percent) and comes off the bottom at 4.57 s still moving: it curves round in front of the floor, below TOTAL's base, and heads right with no stop, rises to the floor line past TOTAL, goes behind the C block at 5.33 s (the block gets a nudge) and stops against the pencil's foot at 6.1 s (0.3 s pause). The climb, six small steps: onto the C block's top (6.83 s, the block dips), the green slab's right end (7.33 s, the slab dips), three steps up the purple bar (7.77, 8.17 and 8.57 s) and back onto the block with a small hop (9.03 s; the block tips a little under it), then it rolls to its spot as the block settles and the teeter starts again at 9.7 s. The ball turns as it rolls (Chapter 1 card 1 audited too, see the room 1 note). Adapted to the art: the bar's high end is under the top block, so the ball lands on the bar at x 769; the bar rests on the white joint, so the joint squashes as the ball crosses it and again when it touches its shoulder (in front of the bar's end, for 3 frames); the pencil is the wall that turns the ball back from the bar's low end to the stick; TOTAL's left edge is the only open slide, and it ends on the floor at the left, so to head right without a stop or crossing in front of the card the ball swings round in a curve in front of the floor line, below the base (the ball's floor clip is removed for this), and the C block stands in front of the ball (it runs behind it, hidden for about 0.2 s; the block's nudge is the tap); there is no free spot at the slab ends (the joint and the pencil are against them), so the climb touches down there for 4 frames in front of the joint instead of resting; the last step is 18 high, the smallest that clears the block's corner. The ball's highest point is y 409 (402 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 151 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the teeter (3 rocks), the curve in front of the floor, the hop heights, the pause, how hard each piece reacts.

**Card 3: the #1 mug circuit** (finesse round 4, 2026-11-02; loop 258 frames, 4.3 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, and each later loop repeats them 4.3 s apart). The ball starts hidden inside the mug (a clip hides it below the mug's front rim) and the journey starts inside the intro as soon as the pan has landed: the mug rocks at 1.62 s and the ball hops out at 1.75 s in one quick flight (0.67 s) over the left white post to the yellow band, which is straight at rest and sags under the ball when it lands at 2.42 s; the band springs back straight and sends the ball on at 2.62 s. It flies (0.57 s) to the leaning books and ricochets off their right face at 3.18 s (they knock back a little and settle), flies to the FIRST card and ricochets off its left edge at 3.78 s (the card wobbles), drops onto the blue stick at 4.35 s, rolls down it (the stick barely flexes), rolls over the white joint at its low end at 5.08 s, falls into the mug at 5.45 s (the mug wobbles on its base) and waits out of sight about 0.5 s before the mug rocks and the ball hops out again (second pass 6.03 s). The ball turns as it rolls (clockwise rolling right, anticlockwise rolling left), keeps its spin in the air and gets a little spin on each ricochet; the turn that is left over at the end of the loop is taken up while the ball is hidden in the mug. The shelf and the posts do not move. Adapted to the art: the stick's low end is right at the mug's rim, so the ball rolls over its end joint and falls into the mug; the hop out of the mug has to rise 260 px to the band, so it is quick but not low (gravity about 0.58, the others about 0.2); the loop is 4.3 s, not 5 s, because each flight is 0.5 to 0.67 s and the mug wait is 0.5 s. The ball's highest point is y 423 (416 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 165 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the length of the loop (the roll down the stick and the wait in the mug are the easy places to add time), how hard the band and the books react.

**Card 4: a streak of hops** (finesse round 2, 2026-11-02; loop 400 frames, 6.7 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes). The ball arrives sitting on the crossword flower, carried in by the pan. Loop: it rests there 3.2 to 4.4 s (the stem sways a little under it), then hops flower head to flower head on an even 0.73 s beat (0.67 s in the air, 0.07 s on the flower): crossword flower to the yellow S hexagon (lands 5.07 s), to the purple leaf (5.8 s), home to the crossword flower (6.53 s), and once more round (7.27, 8.0 and 8.73 s), then rests. Each flower dips and tilts as it is landed on and springs back. The hops are as low as the art allows: the hop from the hexagon to the leaf has to clear the crossword head. The ball's highest point is y 439 (432 px on the phone frame, 181 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: one round or two, the beat, the heights, how far each flower dips.

**Card 5: the ball moves between the tile tops while hidden.** Inside the loop the ball goes from one tile top to the next in a single frame (x 877 to 745 at frames 60 to 61, and 617 to 875 at frames 90 to 91) and the wrap now closes: the ball slides from x 875 back to 618 over frames 177 to 179, behind the letter tiles (global pass 3, 2026-11-02; it was a 257-unit jump at the wrap before). All three moves happen with the ball out of sight behind the tiles, so none shows. If the ball should visibly travel between the tops, that is a finesse call.

**Card 1: pieces outside the safe area** (x 560 to 935, y 0 to 812; found in the global pass, nothing moved, a room-by-room call): the Mouse and its Mouse Hole Clip (x 958 to 984, y 697 to 711), the Mouse Hole (x 1069 to 1090, y 692 to 712) and the Outlet (x 930 to 944, y 681 to 703), all past the right line. They are the pieces the ball passes as it rolls off the right edge, which is part of its story.
